scored_papers.title: Validation of harmonic-space likelihood methods for LiteBIRD B-mode polarisation analysis
scored_papers.abstract: The LiteBIRD satellite mission aims to measure the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ with unprecedented sensitivity through observations of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) $B$-mode polarisation. Robust constraints on $r$ require accurate likelihood modelling across a wide range of angular scales. In this work, we validate harmonic-space likelihood methods against pixel-based benchmarks using 20\,000 end-to-end simulations that include CMB, instrumental noise, and Galactic foreground residuals processed through a realistic component-separation pipeline. We compare a debiased pixel-based likelihood, which serves as our benchmark on large scales ($\ell\leq32$), with an offset Hamimeche \& Lewis (oHL) likelihood applicable across the full multipole range. We systematically explore the space of analysis settings, identifying the number of simulations used for covariance estimation and the choice of beam window function as the most critical factors. Over the full multipole range considered ($\ell\leq128$), where the benchmark combines the pixel-based likelihood at $\ell\leq32$ with a harmonic one at smaller scales, the 68\% upper bound on $r$ from the oHL likelihood is $19$--$29\%$ larger than the benchmark one, depending on the beam window function. This demonstrates its viability as a computationally efficient baseline for LiteBIRD data analysis and cosmological inference from the polarisation $B$-mode field.
scored_papers.reason: 🛰️🎯 LiteBIRD の B モード解析そのもの！2万本の end-to-end シミュレーションで調和空間の尤度を検証していて、r の制約の作り方を知るのにど真ん中の一本🔥
scored_papers.summary: 📊 前景残差込みの成分分離後マップで、低ℓのピクセル尤度を基準に offset 型の調和空間尤度を比較。ℓ≤128 で r の 68% 上限は基準より 19–29% 大きく、共分散のシミュ数とビーム窓関数が鍵📈

scored_papers.title: CosmoForge II. An exact treatment of arbitrary linear filters in quadratic maximum-likelihood power spectrum estimation
scored_papers.abstract: Ground-based cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiments filter their time-ordered data to remove $1/f$ noise and ground pickup, which removes or mixes the large angular scales where primordial $B$ modes peak. A common remedy is a pseudo-$C_\ell$ estimator with harmonic $B$-purification and a transfer function measured from simulations. Another applies it after a matrix-based $E/B$ purification of the maps. We extend the quadratic maximum-likelihood (QML) estimator of CosmoForge to filtered maps, treating the filter exactly: a linear filter conjugates the estimator's ingredients without altering its structure. The same holds for the pixel-based likelihood of CosmoForge, which gives the smallest error bar achievable on the same maps. We compare all methods in a simplified setup under several map-level filters through the error bars on bandpowers and on the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. QML sits $2$ to $4\%$ above the pixel-likelihood bound on $\sigma (r)$ in every filter state. At low noise, the pure pseudo-$C_\ell$ $\sigma (r)$ is $1.21$ times QML's without filtering, $3.0$ times under a scan filter along stripes of constant declination, and $3.7$ times under one from a toy constant-elevation scan. The matrix-purified pseudo-$C_\ell$ $\sigma (r)$ is at most $1.03$ times QML's except under the constant-elevation filters, where it reaches $1.10$. These factors shrink towards unity at higher noise. The pure pseudo-$C_\ell$ gap comes from apodisation and from harmonic $E/B$ separation; pixel-space separation closes it, except under the constant-elevation filters, which attenuate modes rather than remove them and widen the gap. QML stays within a few per cent of the optimal error bars without the tuning and simulated transfer functions of the pseudo-$C_\ell$ pipelines. Thus, CosmoForge provides a robust framework for power-spectrum estimation and inference on filtered maps. (Abridged)
scored_papers.reason: 🧹📡 地上 CMB の時系列フィルタが大角度の B モードを削る問題に、QML 推定でフィルタを厳密に扱う手法！擬 Cℓ との誤差比較が具体的で、r の推定パイプラインの理解に効く✨
scored_papers.summary: 📐 線形フィルタは QML 推定量の構造を変えず成分を共役変換するだけと示し、σ(r) はピクセル尤度の限界の 2–4% 以内。純粋な擬 Cℓ は走査フィルタ下で最大 3.7 倍悪化する📊

scored_papers.title: The Simons Observatory: Frequency-resolved beam calibration for the SO SATs with POLOCALC
scored_papers.abstract: We present a far-field beam calibration of the Simons Observatory (SO) Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) using scanned single-frequency measurements of a drone-mounted source emitting in the 90 GHz band, where the SATs have an angular resolution of $\sim$30$'$. We then compare the results from two campaigns in April and December 2025 to the band-averaged beams from planet observations by the SATs. Measuring the telescope beam response at different frequencies across the observing bands enables modeling the system's frequency-dependent behavior. This helps track optical non-idealities. The comparison with planet beams informs the frequency resolution necessary to accurately reconstruct the band-averaged beams in this way; it uses only the average drone and planet products, as it is intended to demonstrate the feasibility of the frequency-resolved calibration scheme rather than to set the precise beam covariance and instrument requirements. We find that the beams of the two SATs near 90 GHz follow the frequency scaling expected for diffraction-limited optics, with only modest deviations observed in the nearest lobes of one telescope. We establish consistency between the real band-averaged planet beams and the synthesized drone band-averaged beams for the center wafers of both telescopes, with an average deviation smaller than 4% for multipoles $\ell < 500$.

scored_papers.title: TDCOSMO 2026: new insights on the Hubble tension from strong lensing time delays
scored_papers.abstract: We discuss the measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) in flat $\Lambda$ cold dark matter cosmology based on the blind hierarchical analysis of 11 multiply-imaged quasars (hereafter the TDCOSMO-2026 sample) and described in greater detail in a companion paper. In addition to the time delays, we use lens models based on high-resolution imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), analyzed jointly with axisymmetric dynamical models based on JWST-NIRSpec, VLT-MUSE, and Keck-KCWI spectroscopy. Our primary result $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$ is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with $\Omega_{\rm m}$ constraints from the DES-Dovekie supernova (SN) dataset. Our 3% precision accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. Importantly, our measurement is independent of the local distance ladder (LDL). Among individual late-universe probes, only the traditional LDL is more precise. We discuss our result in the context of the Hubble tension, the difference between $H_0$ measured in the late universe and the prediction based on early-universe probes such as the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We construct combinations of independent late-universe probes and show that the tension with the Planck CMB prediction is robust to excluding any one of the methods based on Type-Ia Supernovae, Cepheids, or the Tip of the Red Giant Branch. For example, we construct a 'no-SN' $H_0$ measurement, by replacing the DES-Dovekie constraint on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ with that from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations, and then combining TDCOSMO-2026 with independent non-SN late-universe probes. This 'no-SN' late-universe probe is in 3.7$\sigma$ tension with Planck. Even after completely excluding the LDL, the tension with Planck persists at the 2.7$\sigma$ level.
scored_papers.reason: 🔭⚖️ 強重力レンズの時間遅延で H0 を 3% 精度で測った最新結果！距離はしごに頼らず、超新星を除いても Planck との張力が残るという話は H0 張力を追うなら必読🔥
